subject: Urgent: Zenora production perf hit after quant profile v2 - rollback request
body:
From: Lucas Cheng <lucas@zenora.ai>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priya.kapoor@zenora.ai
Date: 2026-09-30 09:15 PDT
Subject: Sudden P99 spike + errors after v2 quant profile rollout

Hi Lauren,

We pushed Redwood's recommended quant_profile_v2 to production yesterday (09/29) and since early this morning we’re seeing a huge degradation: P99 latency up ~2.4x, throughput down ~40% for our long-context routes, and a 3% error rate (502s and timeouts). This started for a subset of requests after the rollout and correlates with the new profile. Our Pod autoscaler couldn’t keep up and we hit throttles.

We’ve attached a sampling of error payloads and a latency plot. This is impacting our checkout flow — trying to get a mitigation plan ASAP. Can we pause/rollback the profile?

Lucas
VP Engineering, Zenora AI

---

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: Lucas Cheng <lucas@zenora.ai>, priya.kapoor@zenora.ai
Date: 2026-09-30 09:35 PDT
Subject: Re: Sudden P99 spike + errors after v2 quant profile rollout

Hi Lucas / Priya — thanks for the quick flag and the attachments. I’m escalating on our side and will get a mitigation plan to you in the hour. Short version: we’ll canary a rollback to the previous quant profile and enable an automatic fallback to the float32 variant for requests above 2k tokens, plus increase CPU-side request queue to help throughput.

I’ve looped in our infra and performance leads and attached next steps. I’ll follow up with a concrete rollback time window — want to avoid any data loss but prioritize availability.

— Lauren
Head of Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference

---

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-30 10:05 PDT
Subject: URGENT: Zenora production — quant_profile_v2 regression (need rollback & exec brief)

Team —

Zenora (VIP, high-usage customer) reports major perf and error regressions after our quant_profile_v2 rollout. Key customer impact: P99 latency +140% vs baseline on long-context routes, throughput ~40% lower, and 3% error rate producing checkout failures. They attached p99 plot and errors (attached). Customer is asking to pause/rollback immediately.

Action items:
- Neha: please prioritize a root-cause triage (perf counters, kernel selection, KV-cache behaviour) and confirm whether this is due to kernel path selection for int4 paths on A10X vs expected fallback. Include profiling for token-length buckets (<=512, 512-2k, >2k).
- Marcus: prepare rollback instructions and a canary rollback plan (single region, 10% traffic, 30 min observation window), and estimate MTTR.
- Markus: prepare a short exec note summarizing customer impact + suggested credits/contract levers if rollback causes transient errors. I’ll need this for a quick exec sync if Zenora escalates to their board.

Please treat this as P1 — ping me over Slack for synchronous coordination.

Thanks,
Lauren

---

From: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-09-30 11:20 PDT
Subject: Re: URGENT: Zenora production — quant_profile_v2 regression (initial findings)

Quick update from triage:
- Reproduced on our staging with the same traffic mix. The regression appears when requests hit >1.5k token KV-cache lines; the int4 kernel chooses a different matmul tiling which increases kernel latency for sparse attention patterns.
- There’s also an unexpected memory-copy path that fires for >2k tokens causing additional tail latency.
- Error samples are timeouts thrown by the request queue after increased per-request latency; not model hallucinations.

Attachments: quant_profile_v2.yaml (the profile pushed), p99_latency_plot.png (customer), error_rate_samples.zip (logs).

Immediate recommendation: rollback quant_profile_v2 to quant_profile_v1 for production while we patch the tiling/kernel selection. I can prepare a mitigated v2' that forces fallback to the previous kernel for long-context requests.

I’ll continue profiling and will share a short RCA draft by EOD.

-Neha
Principal Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

---

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: Lucas Cheng <lucas@zenora.ai>, Priya Kapoor <priya.kapoor@zenora.ai>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-01 08:00 PDT
Subject: Action plan: temporary rollback + monitoring window (Zenora)

Lucas / Priya —

Thanks again for the data. Based on our triage, recommendation is to rollback to quant_profile_v1 to restore baseline latency and throughput while we ship a targeted fix. Proposed plan:

1) Canary rollback: 2026-10-02 02:00 UTC (scheduled window) — rollback 10% traffic in us-west-2, monitor P95/P99 and error-rate for 30 minutes.
2) If stable, increase to 50% and then 100% in 2-hour increments.
3) We will enable automatic fallback to float32 for requests >2k tokens during the window to avoid KV-copy path triggering.
4) We’ll provide live monitoring links and invite your ops on the call.

Can you confirm availability for the 02:00 UTC window? If you prefer earlier, we can attempt a now rollback but would need your signoff for risk.

We’ll attach a concise rollback_plan.md and keep you updated.

— Lauren

---

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com, markus.klein@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2026-10-05 16:12 PDT
Subject: Final: Zenora rollback scheduled + exec note request (need approval for credits)

Team —

Status: Zenora accepted the 02:00 UTC rollback window. Neha, your patch that forces kernel fallback for >2k tokens is in review; Marcus, rollback steps look good and we've rehearsed the playbook. We’ll run the canary 02:00 UTC on 10/02 as planned.

Zenora is requesting a goodwill credit for the incident and expedited SLA reporting to their board. Markus — please draft a short exec summary and the proposed credit (recommendation: one month of committed usage credit scaled to their average consumption) so I can brief leadership.

I’ve attached rollback_plan.md and included the JIRA ticket INF-2310 in the doc links. If leadership approves the credit, I will communicate the resolution and next steps to Lucas/Priya and confirm the full rollback completion timeline.

Thanks — and please mark items you own as done in the JIRA.

Lauren
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 11:00 AM PDT, neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> FYI I pushed the v2' branch with the kernel-forced-fallback patch to staging; perf looks back to baseline in our load tests. Will open the PR with test logs.
